newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on soybean drop, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on soybean drop, exports.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a decline in nearby soybeans and on export concerns, traders said.
News Japan bought corn from China rather than from the U.S. also weighed on the market.
Japan bought 7,400 tonnes of corn from China for May and July shipment and Tokyo traders indicated they would buy more corn from China if the prices were competitive.
USDA's weekly export sales report is slated for release at 0730 CDT Thursday and there were estimates the corn net export sales tally may come in as low as 250,000 tonnes, they said.
But the consensus was for corn exports Thursday to range from 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
Corn was underpinned by cold, wet weather in the northern U.S. Midwest which could delay seeding of the crop.

Refco Inc sold three million bushels of December and sold 2.5 million July, traders said. The Chicago Corp sold 2.5 million July and sold one million December and LIT America sold two million bushels of July, floor sources said.
Funds sold at least 10 million bushels Wednesday.
Corn closed 1/2 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 1/2 at $2.99 a bushel.

In spread trading, Cargill Investor Services did one million December/July at 11-1/2 to 12 cents, premium July and Cargill Inc did 1.5 million July/May at 2-3/4 to three cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn volume was estimated by the CBOT at 60,000 contracts, above Tuesday's volume of 54,425 contracts.

In corn options, The Chicago Corp sold 500 July $2.90 puts at 8-1/4 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 400 May $3.00 calls at four cents and Farmers Commodities Corp bought 400 July $2.90 puts at 8-1/2 cents and sold 800 July $2.70 puts at 2-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, above the 14,404 traded Tuesday.
